ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a large park with an irregular outer boundary, divided by internal curves into 9 regions, and the regions are labeled 12, 3, 11, 4, 7, 6, 10, 9, 4 respectively. The region on the left outer boundary is labeled 12, the top region is labeled 11, the small middle region is labeled 4, the lower-left nearby region is labeled 7, the bottom-left region is labeled 6, the large middle-right region is labeled 10, the region on the right outer boundary is labeled 9, and the lower-right region is labeled 4. Reasoning: Group according to the specified alternating-coloring cancellation method. Take group A as {12, 11, central 4, 6, 9, lower-right 4}, and group B as {3, 7, 10}. Each number represents the perimeter of that region. When adding the perimeters of group A and subtracting the perimeters of group B, common internal boundaries are positive in one adjacent group and negative in the other, canceling each other out; while the outer boundary of the whole park is contributed only by regions in group A, so it remains. Therefore the perimeter of the whole park is (12 + 11 + 4 + 6 + 9 + 4) - (3 + 7 + 10) = 46 - 20 = 26 km.

method.method_draft: Use an alternating-color cancellation argument. From the image, identify the nine labeled sections and their adjacencies. Color the regions in two groups so that every shared internal boundary lies between opposite colors and every section touching the outside boundary is in the same color group: one valid grouping is A = {12, 11, central 4, 6, 9, lower-right 4} and B = {3, 7, 10}. From the text, use that each number is the perimeter of that section in km. Add the perimeters in group A and subtract the perimeters in group B. Internal shared borders cancel because they are counted once in each color group, while the outer boundary remains because it is adjacent only to group A sections. Compute (12 + 11 + 4 + 6 + 9 + 4) - (3 + 7 + 10) = 46 - 20 = 26 km.
